name: British Virgin Islands
summary_text: British Virgin Islands: own legal system; decriminalised; conservative tight-knit island society, thin institutional cover. Scored as a dependent jurisdiction: the parent framework governs what a visitor encounters, plus local society and enforcement. Score re-anchored 2026-09-24: United Kingdom (0.48) plus a local delta of -0.06. This jurisdiction was not covered by the dedicated state/province research passes.

sources.title: Judge rules Scottish guidance for housing trans prisoners is unlawful - BBC News
sources.claim_summary: NOTE: This BBC article is about Scotland's prison policy for trans prisoners (June 2026 ruling), not the British Virgin Islands; included as UK-context material (the BVI is a British Overseas Territory).

sources.title: Suicide risk if trans prisoners are put in jails based on sex at birth, court told - BBC News
sources.claim_summary: NOTE: This BBC article is about the same Scottish prison-housing litigation (Feb 2026), not the BVI; included as UK-context material only.

sources.title: Gay rights map: Notes on the data - BBC News
sources.claim_summary: BBC News (Feb 2014): 'Gay rights map: Notes on the data' - the BBC/UN OHCHR gay-rights map and timeline methodology built on ILGA data (context for the British Virgin Islands as a UK territory).

AP (Jan 2001): Britain scrapped homosexuality laws in its five Caribbean territories (including the British Virgin Islands) via Privy Council order after local legislatures refused; BVI legislator Orlando Smith: 'There is nothing we can do about it.'

sources.title: Gay Life in British Virgin Islands - GlobalGayz
sources.claim_summary: GlobalGayz 'Gay Life in British Virgin Islands' (Aug 2012/2017): the BVI and USVI are 'among the more gay welcoming islands in the Caribbean, but are not without resistance and secret lives'; most native homophobia is 'silent and invisible' and most tourists hardly notice.

sources.title: Christian Council loses appeal bid in same-sex marriage case
sources.claim_summary: BVI News (July 2022): the BVI Christian Council lost its proposed appeal in the case of Kinisha Forbes and Kirsten Lettsome - a couple married in the UK seeking recognition of their marriage under BVI law and a ruling that the same-sex marriage prohibition is unconstitutional; Judge Jack ruled the appeal had 'no realistic prospect of success'.
